title: PCA — Principal Component Analysis
summary: PCA is a technique that compresses many correlated variables into a few new ones (principal components) that keep most of the information.
how_it_is_used: In Chequi we use PCA to explore the climate data and find patterns between municipalities and variables. It is an exploratory step; it helps us understand the data before training predictive models.
key_takeaways: Reduces dozens of variables to a handful of components.
Does not predict by itself; it supports analysis.

title: XGBoost — Gradient Boosted Trees
summary: XGBoost is a machine learning algorithm that combines many small decision trees to make accurate predictions from tabular data.
how_it_is_used: We use XGBoost to predict, for the next day, the probability of rain and the minimum temperature, per municipality. Only the models that beat a climate baseline are kept in production.
key_takeaways: Works well with the tabular climate features we build.
Only the rain occurrence and minimum temperature (next day) models are active.

title: Walk-forward validation
summary: Walk-forward validation trains the model only on past data and tests it on future data, moving the window forward year by year.
how_it_is_used: We use walk-forward folds from 2023 to 2026 to estimate how well each model will perform on future days. This mirrors real operation, where the model can never see the future.
key_takeaways: Respects the time order of the data.
Compares the model against climate baselines.
Skill > 0 means the model beats the baseline.

title: SHAP — Feature Attribution
summary: SHAP explains each prediction by attributing how much each input feature pushed the result up or down.
how_it_is_used: For each forecast we can show why the model predicted a colder or warmer night, or a higher or lower chance of rain. This makes the tool easier to trust and audit.
key_takeaways: Supports auditing and communication with users.
